messages:
Customer Rep (ACME): Hi team — ACME reporting big regression since ~2026-11-02T14:00Z. p99 for POST /v1/generate jumped from ~120ms to ~800ms. They've opened ticket #8921 and asked for a timeline and mitigation.
Maria: Sorry about that. I'm pulling the lines now. Can you share a sample request id or trace id from their failed calls? Any change on ACME side?
Customer Rep (ACME): Trace ids: trace=01ab3f2c, 01ab3f7d. No config changes on our end. They say it coincided with your "auth-cache" deploy yesterday.
AlertsBot: [ALERT] service/redwood-inference.prod: p99 latency increased to 780ms (start 2026-11-02T14:03Z). Affected route: /v1/generate. AlertID: a-4512. Link: https://alerts.internal/alerts/a-4512
Jace: I can see the spike on infra dashboards. Quick question for clarity: are we comparing raw histogram p99s or rollup/aggregated p99? Rollups over 1m windows will amplify short spikes.
Ethan: Heads up — we changed the auth cache TTL default in yesterday's deploy to reduce stale tokens. That increased KMS verifications for some tenants before the cache warmed. Investigating whether ACME fell into the cold bucket.
Maria: @Customer Rep (ACME) can you run this quick reproducer and paste response headers + latency?
Maria: ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
Customer Rep (ACME): Ran that against a sample key — response header x-request-id: 01ab3f7d, x-server-latency: 812ms, got a couple of 401->retry entries in the logs. Attached snippet.
Jace: Looking at the traces for 01ab3f7d: we see initial auth validation calls out to KMS which take ~300ms. Then client retry path triggers an extra KMS check adding ~300ms more — two retries push total to ~900ms for the tail. That matches ACME's p99. Also our dashboard panel is a 1m rollup which shows the worst-outlier buckets more prominently.
Ethan: Short-term mitigations: 1) temporarily bump auth-cache TTL for ACME to avoid KMS roundtrips, 2) enable a warm-cache job for their tenant, or 3) rollback the TTL change. Medium-term: add local token verification to avoid sync KMS calls on every request and add jittered backoff on retry path.
Maria: I've filed internal escalation (ENG-1129) and requested ops to apply a TTL bump for ACME. Notifying account team and marking support ticket #8921 updated. :thumbsup:
Jace: For the observability dispute: I'll add an annotation to the dashboard explaining rollup vs raw histogram differences and open a ticket to surface raw histogram queries for customers (INF-642). That should reduce confusion when p99 appears inflated due to aggregation windows.
Ethan: I'll apply the temporary TTL bump now and monitor p95/p99 for the next 2 hours. If p99 remains high after mitigation we can consider rollback.
AlertsBot: [RESOLVED] p99 returned to baseline (~130ms) at 2026-11-02T15:05Z for /v1/generate. AlertID: a-4512.
Customer Rep (ACME): ACME confirms performance is back to normal. Thanks for the fast triage.
Maria: Thanks everyone. Will follow up in ENG-1129 with postmortem and next steps (warm-cache + observability note).
